title: Player Journey and Demo Flow
summary: Maps a 20–30 minute reviewer journey through nine beats, teaching mechanics through play while escalating curiosity into confrontation.
sourceFile: Vertical Slice/02 - Player Journey and Demo Flow.docx

entering an unknown world, progressively understanding its environment, forming a strategy through characters and elements, discovering that initial appearances do not tell the whole story, and culminating in a confrontation that uses everything learned along the way.

Before moving this document to APPROVED, we must decide:
The Player Journey can be considered validated when:
a new player completes the demo without external help;
executes at least one reaction before the Strong Encounter;
reaches the Boss without major confusion;
knows why the local story ended;
recognizes that a larger mystery remains.
At the end of each test, we should ask:
Which mechanic did you like the most?
Did you remember that you could swap characters?
Did you understand what triggered the reactions?
Did you know when to dodge?
Did you feel free to explore?
Did you know where to go?
What did you think was happening at first?
What question were you left with?
Did you understand when it could take damage?
The Player Journey works when the tutorial gradually disappears and, by the end:
the Boss forces the player to spontaneously use what they learned without the game having to remind them.
That would be our small “click” moment.
the player sees Zalenquea raise its arm, recognizes the telegraph, dodges, swaps character, triggers a reaction, and punishes the opening.
At that moment, the Vertical Slice stops being a PowerPoint presentation with buttons.
It starts to become a video game.
